heartbeat.title: Mirror the mind, don't push the offer
heartbeat.body_html: The clearest signal across this month's 11 winning tests is that subject lines echoing the subscriber's own state beat lines that lead with pressure. Question openers like "Still deciding?" on Abandoned Cart, open-loop ellipses on Bounce Back, and decision-framed social proof on Abandoned Checkout all won by meeting the reader where they are before the offer appears. We are now carrying that self-recognition frame into the next round of subject line tests across the recovery flows, so a lesson learned in one place keeps paying off in others.

narrative.html: Flows earned $192,597, up 6.9% versus July. That is 25.2% of total store revenue, matching last month at the top of the 12-month range and well above where the year began.
Flows are the most efficient per-email channel we run. Flow revenue per email delivered was $0.286, and at $0.022 for campaigns flows earned 13.0x more per email sent.

Campaigns added the second lever. We sent 31 campaigns this month; together flows and campaigns split email revenue 73% flows to 27% campaigns, with flows carrying the efficient core and campaigns extending reach on demand.
Deliverability stayed clean. Unsubscribes ran at 0.304% of delivered and spam complaints at 0.001%, keeping the sending reputation that lets both levers land in the inbox.

monthly.title_sub: Flows delivered $192,597 in August, up 6.9% on July and holding a quarter of total store revenue.

heartbeat.title: Emotion beats the discount reminder
heartbeat.body_html: The clearest transferable lesson this month came from the winning copy tests. In both Browse Abandon and Abandoned Cart, replacing a discount-led line with emotional weight and social proof lifted results, and the subscription confirmation won by naming the recurring saving plainly in the subject line. The pattern is consistent: make the mother feel seen and give her a concrete reason to act, rather than repeating an offer. We are already carrying that framing into adjacent flows, which is how the program keeps compounding month after month.

narrative.html: Flows earned $180,184, up 103.0% month over month. Revenue per email delivered rose from $0.269 to $0.339, so each send is working harder, not just sending more.
Flows reached 25.2% of total store revenue, a 12-month high. Across a store that did $714,965 in July, more than a quarter of all revenue came through the automated flows we manage.

Campaigns are the second lever we run. We sent 22 campaigns this month, and together flows and campaigns split email revenue with flows at 71%. Flows remain the most efficient per-email channel we run, earning $0.339 per email against $0.025 for campaigns, or 13.6x per email, which is exactly why we weight effort toward them.
Deliverability stayed clean. Unsubscribes held at 0.23% of delivered and spam complaints at 0.002%, so the extra volume and revenue came without straining list health.

monthly.title_sub: Flows delivered $180,184 in July, up 103.0% on the prior month, and reached a 12-month high of 25.2% of total store revenue.
